paragraphs: Actor Hayden Panettiere, who was known for roles in television’s “Heroes” and “Nashville” and had recently published a memoir, has died, her father said in a statement Sunday night. She was 36. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden,” Skip Panettiere said in a statement provided by her representative. The Greenville County Coroner’s Office said Monday that the cause of death is pending further investigation. An autopsy was completed Monday, the statement added, and “no signs of trauma were discovered that would have contributed to the death.” At around 1:50 p.m. Sunday, authorities received a 911 call about a “reported cardiac arrest” at an apartment complex, according to the coroner’s office. Police said an acquaintance of Panettiere’s made the 911 call. “Panettiere was found unresponsive inside the residence, where she had been temporarily staying,” the coroner’s office said. Advanced cardiac life support measures were initiated, but resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful, the statement added. Panettiere was pronounced dead at 2:32 p.m. “The case is under investigation by the Greenville Police Department in conjunction with the Greenville County Coroner’s Office,” police said Sunday, adding that the preliminary investigation had not indicated any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances. Panettiere revealed this year that she previously struggled with postpartum depression and addiction, which she said led to her decision to give up custody of her only child, daughter Kaya Evdokia Klitschko, in 2018, whom she had with former partner Wladimir Klitschko, the Ukrainian professional boxer. Panettiere recently published a memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” which generated headlines over its revelations, including some about her past relationships. In 2024, she described the pain and grief after her younger brother, actor Jansen Panettiere, died unexpectedly of an undiagnosed heart condition the previous year. “When you lose somebody that you saw in all the important moments in your life, standing right next to you, it just rocks your world,” she told NBC’s “TODAY” show. Panettiere started working at 11 months old, when she appeared in television commercials, it said. She appeared on soap operas, including “One Life to Live” and “Guiding Light,” beginning at age 4. articles.title: Coyote vs. Acme is even funnier because Warner Bros. Discovery tried to kill it
articles.summary: Part of what makes Coyote vs. Acme — in theaters August 28th — work so well is all the melodrama WBD whipped up.
articles.body: There’s an argument to be made that people wouldn’t be all that interested in Coyote vs. Acme if it weren’t for the way David Zaslav tried to kill it. By trying to shelve the project, Warner Bros. Discovery only drew attention to its habit of disappearing nearly completed movies in order to cash in on tax write-offs.  Coyote vs. Acme’s generally positive reviews are on the money; it really is one of the best Looney Tunes movies in years. In theory, this suggests that the movie might do well at the box office and become a case study in WBD making terrible decisions. Ironically, though, all of the drama surrounding the live-action / animated hybrid film is actually part of what makes it an enjoyable watch.  Loosely based on Ian Frazier’s Coyote v. Acme piece in The New Yorker, the new movie follows Wile E. Coyote as he concocts another harebrained scheme to kill the Road Runner. But rather than simply trying to destroy his nemesis with elaborate plans that involve various gadgets, Coyote decides to go after Acme with a lawsuit over its faulty products. Though attorney Kevin Avery (Will Forte) would rather take the settlement proposed by Acme’s legal counsel Buddy Crane (John Cena), Coyote believes he can receive a much bigger payout by going to court. And with countless examples of how Acme’s products have harmed him, Coyote’s confident that he can build a strong case. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kMsiD1Nky5I] Coyote vs. Acme leans into the absurd with a world in which humans and cartoon maniacs exist alongside one another. When the coyote isn’t busy trying to catch his dinner, he has to deal with all the ordinary drudgery that comes with being a productive member of society, like Avery’s niece, Paige (Lana Condor.) This and the way a bevy of Looney Tunes characters pop up as people working regular jobs brings a delightful energy to Coyote vs. Acme that’s akin to The Muppets. And by framing Acme as a cross between WBD, Apple, Tesla, and Lockheed Martin, the movie sets its story up to work as commentary about corporations screwing customers over with false promises. At its core, Coyote vs. Acme is a classic Looney Tunes project, meaning that it spends much of its runtime focusing on ridiculous gags. The movie’s script — penned by James Gunn, Jeremy Slater, and Samy Burch — features moments where Coyote and Avery grow to see one another as friends, but it’s mostly focused on showcasing how chaotic life would be in a world filled with beings who regularly defy the laws of physics with their cartoonish antics. This makes Coyote vs. Acme an excellent showcase of the way its creative team blends traditional animation with live-action footage. The movie’s set pieces are mildly amusing, but its story is so by-the-numbers that one would be hard-pressed to call it riveting. What is interesting about the film’s story is the way it makes WBD seem like a studio that’s afraid of poking fun at itself. You can almost hear Gunn, Slater, and Burch having a laugh at Zaslav’s expense as Foghorn Leghorn (Eric Bauza) is introduced as Acme’s conniving leader, and those kinds of jokes are what makes the movie feel like it might actually resonate with audiences. By going meta and not exactly trying to be a movie for children (remember, this is about a legal battle), Coyote vs. Acme highlights how WBD could be getting a bit more use out of characters like Bugs Bunny (also Bauza) and Granny (Candi Milo). Had the studio just put the movie out on its own, it might have made Zaslav and his fellow executives seem like people with an understanding of how to capitalize on legacy intellectual property. But whatever accolades Coyote vs. Acme ultimately receives will largely be attributed to Ketchup Entertainment, which bought the rights to distribute it. The box office performances for WBD’s last few Looney Tunes projects suggests that Coyote vs. Acme won’t be breaking any records before it winds up on one streaming platform or another. But when the film releases on August 28th, it will remind the public of how ready WBD was to throw it in the chipper. Especially now as the studio navigates a potential merger with Paramount, that kind of cavalier attitude toward jettisoning people’s work makes Zaslav’s WBD seem like a company that isn’t exactly committed to art. That might not matter to Zaslav, who stands to make bank regardless of whether the Paramount merger goes through. But it’s a terrible look for a studio that’s trying to maintain its reputation as one of Hollywood’s biggest players.

articles.title: ‘Dune: Part Three’ sets off early ticket frenzy as fans crash sales sites
articles.summary: Fans eager to see “Dune: Part Three” on the biggest screens in December first had to survive the online ticket queue.
articles.body: Fans eager to see “Dune: Part Three” on the biggest screens in December first had to survive the online ticket queue. Many on social media reported long waits and ticketing site crashes Tuesday as they scrambled to snag seats for early IMAX 70 mm screenings in December. “Am I tripping or did every website for Dune 3 IMAX 70MM crash?” an X user wrote. “Help! Has anybody beaten this bug/error to secure Dune 3 tickets???” another person asked, sharing a screenshot of the Fandango site with a message that read: “Internal server error. Please try again.” “I HAVE THREE DEVICES OPEN TRYING TO GET DUNE TICKETS AND NONE OF THEM WORK,” another X user said. The rollout is the latest sign of a growing frenzy around seeing major movies in specific premium formats, in which securing the right seat and screen has become an event of its own. A similar rush unfolded in June, when advance sales for Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” overwhelmed AMC’s website, with some moviegoers reporting hourslong waits. “Dune: Part Three” is the latest installment in Warner Bros. Pictures’ adaptation of Frank Herbert’s seminal 1965 novel set thousands of years in the future in a world devastated by ecological collapse. The movie, directed by Denis Villeneuve, picks up 17 years after the previous one, with Paul Atreides (played by Timothée Chalamet) ruling the galaxy while in a political marriage to Princess Irulan (Florence Pugh). The sci-fi franchise, which also stars Zendaya and Jason Momoa, has become an audience must-see since the first installment’s box-office success in 2021. Though the new film isn’t being released until Dec. 18, some fans had already bragged about getting their tickets in April when IMAX first released a limited number of tickets for some screenings. Last week, IMAX sent out an email telling fans to “Save the Date” for another chance to get early tickets. “Dear IMAX fans, You showed up in a big way when the first DUNE: PART THREE tickets were released,” the email read. “We’ve heard you and know you want more access to tickets and more time to plan. So, here you go... The next opportunity to get DUNE: PART THREE tickets will arrive in one week on Tuesday, August 18 at 9:00 a.m. PST. This ticket drop will unlock more opening week DUNE Insider Screenings in IMAX and IMAX 70mm, so mark your calendars, make your plans, and get ready to return to Arrakis.” By Tuesday, people’s efforts to secure tickets had turned into viral mayhem. Fans reported that at certain points, AMC’s and Fandango’s apps had crashed. (AMC and Fandango did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday.) Several people who managed to get tickets said it took them over an hour of waiting. A person on X posted a picture of a line wrapped around an AMC in New York, where fans tried to secure tickets in person. Some people also began reselling their early tickets on eBay for up to $1,000. The demand for multiformat viewing experiences is fueling moviegoing FOMO, reshaping how studios market tentpole films and prompting an effort to bring order to an increasingly crowded premium-screen landscape. Some frustrated cinephiles argue theater chains and studios should do more to ensure a smoother ticketing process. “If you’re going to turn movie ticket-buying into a competitive sport, then you need to have the tech and UX to support that shift,” film critic Barry Hertz wrote on X. “Theatrical exhibition is not easy, certainly, but it doesn’t need to be this hard.” AMC CEO Adam Aron addressed fan frustration Tuesday on X. He said that “ticketing traffic across AMC’s website and mobile app reached levels approximately three times higher than what we experienced during the Spider-Man: Brand New Day ticket launch, which itself followed strong advance sales for The Odyssey ticket launch before that.” “It’s not that our systems totally failed,” he added. “We have been selling enormous numbers of tickets today, but when any of our customers experience less than our best, it is just not right.” Aron wrote that while there was “much discussion internally” and preparation for the ticket launch, “We thought we were ready, but we weren’t.” The theater chain, Aron said, requires “about $2 million of IT programming resource” to “fully address the issue.” “Of course, that money has been approved already,” he wrote, “and we’ve asked our IT team to move at a whirlwind speed to take whatever steps are needed so that our ticketing systems are — in all situations and in all quantities —again top shelf.”

articles.title: We played The Duskbloods, the Switch 2’s wildest new exclusive
articles.summary: The Duskbloods is the latest game from Elden Ring developer FromSoftware, and it’s launching exclusively on the Switch 2 in 2026.
articles.body: The Duskbloods is a world away from the approachable games Nintendo is known for. But for its next Switch 2 exclusive, the company has partnered with Elden Ring developer FromSoftware on a hardcore multiplayer game about vampires. And after spending a few hours playing through its gothic world at FromSoft’s offices in Tokyo, I’m convinced that The Duskbloods could end up being one of the most important exclusives for Nintendo’s latest console. It’s a notable change for the company. People buy Nintendo consoles for Nintendo games. That’s a generally accepted truth, and also one that’s backed up by data — a quick glance at the bestselling games across platforms like the Switch and Nintendo 3DS reveals expected names like Mario Kart, Pokémon, and Animal Crossing. Titles from outside developers can be an integral part of broadening a platform’s appeal, but that’s something that Nintendo has historically struggled with. Which is what makes The Duskbloods so intriguing. The Duskbloods is not an easy game to describe. In a universe of vampires that spans multiple time periods, eight players, controlling vampiric characters known as the Bloodsworn, descend on a level filled with enemies and gigantic boss creatures. Over the course of several phases the group is whittled down until only a few remain, who must then fight until only one is left. This isn’t a Fortnite-style battle royale, however. Instead, The Duskbloods is designed to mix the thrill of competitive play with the roleplaying fantasy that FromSoft has become known for through games like Dark Souls and Bloodborne. --- [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/The_Duskbloods_12.png?quality=90&strip=all] Read next: FromSoftware can do anything --- Key to this is something that the game calls “virtue.” Essentially, it’s a system that allows you accumulate points over the course of a match by doing just about everything. You can get virtue by collecting the most items, or by killing the most minor enemies, or by taking down boss creatures like a gigantic frog with far too many humanlike teeth. There are virtue points for exploration — the levels are littered with hidden corpses you can discover — and in the later rounds you can get a huge burst of virtue points by defeating other players on specific points of the map, or making a pledge at an altar before another player stops you. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/The_Duskbloods_17.png?quality=90&strip=all] Each match is divided into four phases, and the player count slowly shrinks through what’s known as “the culling.” Basically, if you don’t have enough virtue points by the time a round ends then you’re out. How many points you need depends entirely on how much virtue other players have collected. The idea is that, even if you maybe aren’t the best one-on-one fighter, you can still progress through the game and make it to the final phase, since there are so many different ways to earn points. And aside from the final round, you’ll respawn immediately after dying with your virtue intact, which makes it easier to try things and explore without fear of the game ending. In practice, The Duskbloods can be an overwhelming experience, at least initially. It took me some time to wrap my head around the points system; in most competitive multiplayer games, killing other players is the clearest path to victory. Here, though, that’s not the case, particularly at the beginning. Instead, the early rounds are best spent exploring the map, defeating weaker enemies, and generally strengthening your character by acquiring items and experience. And there’s a lot more to The Duskbloods’ complexity than just the points system. For starters, there are multiple vampiric characters to play as, each of whom has a very different playstyle. In the early version of the game I played — which is the same as the network test that will run later in August — there are six characters to choose from. There’s an aging senator who wields a rapier that doubles as a cane, and who can both summon a prehistoric bird as a ranged attack and temporarily transform into a bloodthirsty dinosaur. There’s a ninja with circular blades, a mysterious man who can shoot columns of fire from a stone embedded in his hand, and an armor-clad weirdo named Zork who carries around an electrified chunk of undersea cable. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/The_Duskbloods_19.png?quality=90&strip=all] Each character plays differently — some are quick and nimble, others lumbering yet powerful — with their own distinct abilities. During each game you can also find and summon companion characters, called kin, which lend help in battle and can also be leveled up over the course of a match. These can be everything from sword-wielding samurai to gigantic wolves. My favorite was a soprano who was also a wrestler, suplexing enemies while singing a song that helped improve my defensive capabilities. You can also turn certain enemies into your minions by sucking their blood and exerting your influence over them. There are random events that can happen — a zeppelin that barrages the level with bombs, a lightning storm that zaps players to random points on the map — as well as “sigils” you can equip that give you a specific and sometimes strange task to perform that can earn you lots of virtue. For instance, a sigil might be based on revenge, and task you with finding a specific player and killing them. Or it might ask you to find the other player who is your character’s lost love and… propose to them in the middle of the match. These are designed to give you both an additional way to earn points in a match and a role to play in the story. I should note that what I played is missing some key features that will be in the final game, most notably the majority of the character customization and story elements, which will be a major part of the appeal for existing FromSoft fans. Similarly, while all of the games I played ended in a fight to the death, there will be other possible win conditions, like the last group of players teaming up to defeat a boss. And all of that is just scratching the surface. There is a lot going on in The Duskbloods. After spending several hours playing the game with other members of the press over the course of two days, I felt like I had just begun to grasp how everything worked. That’s a far cry from the pick-up-and-play nature that has made Nintendo’s online games like Splatoon and Mario Kart such major successes. Those are games that are easy to grasp from the moment you pick up the controller. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/The_Duskbloods_15.png?quality=90&strip=all] But at the same time, The Duskbloods has the potential to do something very significant. With Elden Ring, FromSoft took an extremely intimidating genre of action RPG and opened it up to a new audience by fusing that style of game onto an open world that gave players more choice for how they approached challenges. The result was a massive hit: Elden Ring has sold more than 30 million copies, its expansion Shadow of the Erdtree sold 10 million, and the game is being made into a Hollywood movie. The Duskbloods, meanwhile, is tackling the similarly intimidating field of competitive multiplayer. And while The Duskbloods is still pretty hardcore, it’s designed in a way that attempts to give players things to do even if they can’t win a match. The live-service space may be a disaster right now, but online multiplayer games still make up the bulk of time people spend playing games. And the combination of online play and FromSoft’s renowned fantasy worldbuilding could eventually lure a new type of player to the Switch 2, at a time when dedicated video game platforms are largely struggling. There’s a lot of risk inherent to a game like this. Control developer Remedy Entertainment, for instance, tried something similar with the co-op shooter FBC: Firebreak, and that didn’t end so well. The Duskbloods has the added challenge of launching exclusively on the Switch 2, a platform that’s not yet known for these kinds of multiplayer experiences. But the same things that make the game a risk are also what make it so fascinating. The Duskbloods is unlike anything else in the Switch 2’s lineup — and it could help Nintendo reach players beyond Zelda and Mario fans.

articles.title: FromSoftware can do anything
articles.summary: Elden Ring studio FromSoftware is going down a different path with The Duskbloods, a multiplayer game that’s exclusive to the Nintendo Switch 2.
articles.body: There’s something just a little bit different about FromSoftware’s office in Tokyo. Like with any other successful video game studio, there’s extensive security to get in the door, a minimalist lobby with framed posters from the studio’s most recent releases, and a large glass display case filled with statues from ceremonies ranging from the BAFTAs to The Game Awards. But the hallways are painted black, a fitting theme for a developer known for crafting dark, gothic worlds and a hint at what new creations are lurking inside. While it has largely become known for a singular style of action game — dubbed “Soulslike,” after the massively influential Dark Souls series — FromSoft has steadily continued to try new things, pushing its signature style into new genres. Perhaps the most extreme example of this is the studio’s next release: The Duskbloods, a competitive multiplayer game set in a world of vampires that will be exclusive to the Switch 2 and published by Nintendo when it launches later this year. It’s a new genre, new setting, new platform, and new publisher all rolled into one game. But after Elden Ring, which has sold more than 30 million copies since it launched in 2022, the team at FromSoft now also feels more assured in expanding their horizons. “With the success of Elden Ring, as a company it has definitely allowed us to explore, I wouldn’t say risky ideas, but things that we might not have had the confidence for,” FromSoftware president Hidetaka Miyazaki, who also directed both Elden Ring and The Duskbloods, told me during a recent hands-on event at the studio’s office. [Image: Hidetaka Miyazaki. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Mr.-Miyazaki-Headshot_Vertical-copy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The studio’s rise to this point has been slow and steady. FromSoft’s first release was the dungeon crawling RPG King’s Field in 1994, and while it launched a consistent stream of titles after that — including the cult-hit mech battling Armored Core series — it was more than a decade later when the studio really started making its mark with the release of Demon’s Souls in 2009. Directed by Miyazaki, the game thrust players into a harsh fantasy world, one where death was a constant and the combat was punishing. It was an experience that demanded a lot from players, but also rewarded their patience with thrilling victories and a story that gradually revealed itself. It was an unlikely hit that spawned a new genre of action games, and was followed up by a number of successors, including a trilogy of Dark Souls titles and the Victorian-era-inspired Bloodborne in 2015. Those games were all successes, selling millions of copies, but it wasn’t until Elden Ring that the studio had its first blockbuster hit. The game not only sold well, but spawned a large-scale expansion, a co-op spinoff called Nightreign, and an upcoming film adaptation from A24 and director Alex Garland. Part of what made Elden Ring a hit was that it took what FromSoft had become known for — relentless action, subtle storytelling, and immersive worlds — and translated it into an open-world adventure and gave players more freedom to explore its bleak and beautiful fantastical realm. Even with its signature game style cemented, FromSoft was continuously experimenting. Sandwiched in between the launches of Dark Souls 3 (2016) and Elden Ring (2022) were a pair of one-off games — a solemn VR story called Déraciné in 2018, and a ninja action game called Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice a year later — that showed the studio expanding its range. At the time, Miyazaki, who directed both games, explained FromSoft’s approach to taking on new projects. “I think one of the studio’s characteristics is to embrace wholeheartedly what we feel is interesting; what we perceive to be worthwhile, cool, or beautiful; and to place these ideals at the foundation of the games we make,” he told me in 2019. “Part of those things we feel may deviate slightly from what is considered to have mass appeal. This ‘unorthodox’ nature could well be what ties our games and our culture together.” [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/The_Duskbloods_16.png?quality=90&strip=all] The Duskbloods may seem like a big departure, but it also fits neatly into this philosophy. Over the years, FromSoft had steadily been injecting multiplayer elements into its largely single-player games; in Elden Ring, for instance, you can summon other players to help you in battle. As the studio experimented in this realm, a number of multiplayer-centric ideas were filed away. “There are a lot of ideas that we had wanted to try that didn’t necessarily fit in that context of a single-player game,” Miyazaki said during the Duskbloods preview in Tokyo. “Those pile up over the years.” That eventually culminated into The Duskbloods. Development on The Duskbloods began in 2021 and originated on the first Switch before eventually migrating to its successor. The game consists of matches where eight players, each controlling a vampiric fighter, have to both fight against the monsters prowling the level as well as compete with each other. The combat is faster than a traditional FromSoft game, and the exploration is much more vertical — you can triple-jump your way up large towers — but it also has many of the studio’s telltale characteristics, from its dark, haunting world to the fact that players will die repeatedly. (For more on how The Duskbloods plays, check out my hands-on right here.) But all of those new elements also made the development process difficult, and Miyazaki says that working with Nintendo has been extremely helpful in this regard. “The Duskbloods is a challenging game for us,” he says. “There are a lot of new things in terms of designing the systems and the rules, and it requires a lot of fine-tuning and adjustments, and Nintendo has provided a lot of support in that regard. Things like onboarding and tutorials for players are something that we are historically not great at, so the support they’ve provided in that regard has been very, very good and we think that it’s been a great relationship in that sense.” On a technical level, Miyazaki notes that the team initially struggled with getting The Duskbloods to work on Nintendo’s previous console, so the reveal of the Switch 2 came as something of a relief. “We were definitely very happy when we heard about the Switch 2, because we were thinking, ‘How are we going to do this?’” Miyazaki says. “The Switch 2 came along and all of those problems were solved.” The game is being designed in part to appeal to players who might not traditionally be interested in competitive multiplayer, a genre that can be intimidating to a lot of people. While The Duskbloods does involve fighting against other players, it also gives them other things to do, whether it’s killing minor enemies to gain experience or exploring the landscape in search of helpful items or sidekicks that can aid in battle. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/The_Duskbloods_18.png?quality=90&strip=all] “We really just want as many players to enjoy our games as possible,” Miyazaki says. “Not just having it be solely [player vs. player], but having more indirect ways that you can compete in the match and enjoy it, is definitely something that we wanted to implement to accommodate players. From a role-playing and story aspect as well, we didn’t want it to be something where you had to always win every single match to enjoy the game. We wanted you to be able to unlock aspects of the story and enjoy it at your own pace, even if you’re not necessarily doing great in every match. And if [players] go in wanting to know more about the story and that’s what interests them, that’s great. And as they reveal that and play more of the game, they might find that they do like the PvP more than they thought. We’re hoping that is an entryway.” It might look like a shift in strategy, particularly as the studio’s last two releases have both focused on multiplayer play. But The Duskbloods is actually an extension of how the studio has worked for years: a big departure that builds off of the developer’s previous work in natural ways. It’s still set in a dark fantasy world, it still stars a cast of eclectic weirdos, and it still thrusts players into a space where they have to master complex systems in order to survive. It just puts these ideas in a new, multiplayer-specific context. Because of this, Miyazaki says that The Duskbloods doesn’t necessarily represent any kind of change in how the studio operates. FromSoft has always made whatever it wanted, and Elden Ring’s success has only made it bolder. “We’re not super rigid,” he says. “It’s more just, if we find something that we want to make and we think it’s a great idea, we’ll make it.”

articles.title: Her name is Chanty Beluga. And she’s all over your social media feed.
articles.summary: Whether she’s ordering takeout or introducing herself at a pool party, she’s going to make sure you know her name.
articles.body: She’s going to a restaurant. She’s ordering takeout. She’s getting in an Uber. In every instance, she makes sure to drop her name: Chanty Beluga. Who is this smiling, millennial blond woman whose videos have gone viral on TikTok? And where did that hypnotic and unique name come from? The character is the alter ego of comedian and actor Courtney O’Donnell, who posts TikTok videos of herself as Chanty Beluga. Cheerful and demurely dressed, Chanty Beluga is always finding herself in situations where she has to use her goofy name. She’s checking in at a restaurant, ordering takeout and introducing herself at a pool party. The videos are quick and simple. Just a woman casually saying her ridiculous name, which seems to roll off the tongue and promote repeat listening. The character has already spawned multiple fan accounts on TikTok. “This is so dumb and I see myself becoming rapidly obsessed with it,” one follower commented on a TikTok video of Chanty at a coffee shop. “No notes. Just a woman named Chanty Beluga in situations where she makes her name known.” “Classic Chanty,” another one wrote. “I would die for Chanty Beluga,” another commented. articles.title: 'That is my fault': Suchitra Mohanlal explains why Pranav Mohanlal, Vismaya Mohanlal are not fluent in Malayalam
articles.summary: Suchitra Mohanlal has opened up about Pranav Mohanlal's and Vismaya Mohanlal's familiarity with Malayalam. She also discussed the reasons Vismaya Moha.
articles.body: Suchitra Mohanlal has opened up about Pranav Mohanlal's and Vismaya Mohanlal's familiarity with Malayalam. She also discussed the reasons Vismaya Mohanlal takes time before committing to acting projects.According to Suchitra Mohanlal, both her children spent their school years in boarding schools. Their surroundings also meant they regularly communicated in English. She said this affected their connection with Malayalam as they grew older.In the interview with Can Media, Suchitra Mohanlal also accepted some responsibility for the situation. She revealed, âVismaya is listening to new stories. She needs about three or four months. Since both the children studied in boarding schools, they don't know Malayalam very well. Appu knows it better, though.You can understand that if you watch his first movie. Jeethu didn't give him many dialogues in 'Aadhi'. But because he has done so many movies now and has spoken to everyone on the sets, his Malayalam has improved considerably.Why Vismaya Mohanlal's Malayalam is limitedSuchitra Mohanlal explained that Vismaya Mohanlal entered boarding school much earlier than her brother. Pranav Mohanlal reportedly joined one when he was in sixth grade. Vismaya Mohanlal went to one while she was still in third grade.âMaaya has that particular problem. Appu went to boarding school when he was in sixth grade. Maaya went when she was in third grade. Most of the children studying there were foreigners. They mostly spoke English. Even when they came home, I spoke to them in English. That is my fault.English was also spoken in Suchitra's familySuchitra Mohanlal said English was not unusual in her own family either. She explained, âWhen I was growing up, we siblings also spoke in English to some extent. That's because Daddy speaks half Tamil and half Malayalam. Mummy is completely Malayali. We speak Malayalam with Mummy. With Daddy, we speak all three, that are English, Tamil and Malayalam.âShe also explained that Mohanlal's busy shooting schedule meant he was frequently away from home. As a result, the children had fewer opportunities to regularly communicate with him.Vismaya Mohanlal lacks confidence in MalayalamSuchitra Mohanlal said the family circumstances gradually reduced her children's connection with Malayalam.âThen when the children came along, their uncle (Mohanlal) wasn't at home either. He was mostly away shooting. I would speak to them over the phone when they were at the hostel every week. When they came home, their cousins had also been born and brought up in Madras, so they too spoke in English."She added, âSo, as they grew up, they lost their connection with Malayalam. When they come here, they speak to their father and mother. Other than that, they don't really have any other connections. Maaya can speak Malayalam, but she doesn't have the confidence to speak it. Then there is the slang. Everyone says I myself have a Tamil influence in my speech.âVismaya Mohanlal needs time for movie projectsSuchitra Mohanlal also explained why Vismaya Mohanlal may take longer before taking up a movie. She said, âMaaya reads scripts in English. She says she needs a month to learn the dialogues. That's why it won't happen immediately. Even if a good project comes along, she needs about a month or a month and a half.âVismaya Mohanlal recently made her acting debut with the movie 'Thudakkam'. In the same interview, Suchitra also revealed that her son Pranav has committed to a project, but she doesn't know the details.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Humanoid robots smash Usain Bolt’s 100-meter record
articles.summary: ﻿Literally ‘smashing’ — the bots can’t stop without colliding into a crash pad.
articles.body: The 9.58-second 100-meter dash record set by Usain Bolt in 2009 has been outpaced by Chinese robots participating at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. In a preliminary heat on Saturday, Tiangong Ultra, made by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation ​Center, ran the distance in 9.39 seconds, followed by the Honor-developed Lightning at 9.47 seconds. It’s one of several notable achievements to take place at the event, which can best be described as a sort of annual robot olympics that’s designed to showcase advancements in bipedal bot technology. After launching in 2025, 2,056 robots from 16 countries are participating in this year’s World Humanoid Robot Games, which includes categories for sprinting, jumping, football, boxing, and more. Tiangong Ultra also ran the 400-meter race in 38.16 seconds — beating the 43.03 second world record set by Wayde van Niekerk in 2016. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zbkqhor3EKI] Unlike human athletes, however, these sprinting bots don’t typically get to perform a victory lap after crossing the finish line. Several videos show the robots colliding into cushioned walls at impressive speeds, where they (or the pieces of what’s left of them) get collected and carried away on a stretcher. Watching the various robot models actually run is both amusing and a little unsettling, given the bizarre way they move to dash so quickly.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere's mom disputes her daughter's claim about their painful split: 'I didn't say what she said'
articles.summary: Lesley Vogel opened up about their estrangement and her concerns about Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson.
articles.body:
Hayden Panettiere 's estranged mother, Lesley Vogel, has disputed the late actor's account of the moment she said she wanted to end their professional relationship, denying that she told her daughter, "You owe me."

In her memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning , which was published in May, Panettiere said that while filming the TV show Heroes at 19, she told Vogel she no longer wanted her to be her manager.

"I said to her, 'I don't want us to work together anymore. I just want you to be my mom,'" Panettiere recalled. According to Panettiere, Vogel responded, "You owe me."

The actor said she "remembered" feeling hopeful about the conversation, but said it was "disappointing" when she came to believe her mother was referring to money. "The fact that she didn't care to have a relationship with me was a tough pill to swallow," she added.

Panettiere died on Aug. 16 at 36. Her cause of death has yet to be confirmed.

In a new interview with ABC News , Vogel said she recalled the conversation taking place in Panettiere's trailer, but denied saying the words attributed to her.

"I remember being in her trailer and literally saying nothing," she said. "I knew that day would come — it's not that I didn't expect it — but it was very short, [a] very brief conversation, and then she turned and went to set… I know I didn't say what she said."

Panettiere's death has raised questions about how child stars in the entertainment industry are treated, with Anna Paquin among those who have called for greater protection for young actors.

Panettiere was 11 months old when she first appeared onscreen in a Playskool commercial. She went on to star in numerous TV shows and films — including Heroes , Nashville and two Scream movies — but struggled with drug addiction, postpartum depression and an abusive relationship with her on-and-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson.

Here are the key points that have emerged since Panettiere died.

What was her relationship with her mom, Lesley Vogel?

Panettiere was estranged from her mother, who helped launch her career as a child model and later oversaw her work as a child actor.

In her memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning , Panettiere described Vogel as a "perfectionist" and recalled feeling pressure to succeed from a young age. She alleged that her mother would become angry when she failed to land roles and once superglued a fallen tooth back into her mouth because she feared it could cost Panettiere a job.

Vogel has disputed Panettiere's characterization of her childhood, telling the Daily Mail that she was demanding but did not force her daughter to work or abuse her. "I was strong, definitely, but I was not abusive by any stretch of the imagination," she said.

Vogel said their relationship remained close through much of Panettiere's childhood and adolescence but began to change when her daughter was around 16 or 17. Vogel attributed their later estrangement in part to her attempts to intervene in Panettiere's relationship with her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson.

"I had to go no contact because I could not help her anymore. I could not change this pattern, and believe me, I tried," Vogel said. "I didn't leave because I didn't care about her or didn't love her. I put so much effort in trying to save her. You cannot save someone who doesn't want to be saved."

What was her relationship with her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson?

Panettiere and Hickerson had a turbulent on-and-off relationship that included documented domestic violence. In 2021, Hickerson pleaded no contest to two felony counts of injuring Panettiere and was sentenced to 45 days in jail , probation and domestic violence classes. Hickerson later told TMZ , "I had a lot to drink, and I got physical with her."

Panettiere addressed the allegations publicly in 2020, saying she hoped sharing her experience would "empower others in abusive relationships to get the help they need and deserve." She also said she was "prepared to do my part to make sure this man never hurts anyone again."

In her memoir, Panettiere wrote about her decision to "let go of my resentment" and try to forgive Hickerson. She added, "I needed him to admit his wrongs and change because of them, but I didn't want to traumatize him in an irreversible way."

Months before her death, Panettiere had reportedly taken steps to keep Hickerson away. The New York Times reported, citing two people with direct knowledge, that private security accompanying her book tour in May had instructions not to let Hickerson into events.

"I needed an incredible amount of support and backup in order to make sure that there was no way for him to find his way back in," Panettiere told the podcast On Purpose .

Vogel described her daughter's relationship with Hickerson as codependent, saying, "When Brian came into her life, the changes started to occur. Very early in the game, I thought he's a modern-day gigolo. I know what he's after.

"I would talk to both of them about it. I would say, 'This is a codependent relationship, and it is not healthy for either of you. My sadness is that everything that I did, her father did, friends did, business people did, we could not break that codependent bond. It is so much more powerful than people understand."

Vogel told ABC News, "She knew that Brian was toxic. She knew she had to get him out of her life."

Hickerson has not been accused of a crime in connection with Panettiere's death.

Hickerson addressed Panettiere's death through his attorney, Sloan Ellis, saying, "Hayden's death remains under investigation, and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed.

"As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play. Out of respect for Hayden's loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time."

What was her relationship with the father of her child, Wladimir Klitschko?

Panettiere dated boxer Wladimir Klitschko on and off between 2009 and 2018. They got engaged in 2013 , but never married, and their daughter, Kaya, was born in 2014. Panettiere was open about her struggles with alcohol and depression, including postpartum depression after Kaya's birth.

Kaya, who is 11, lives with Klitschko in Ukraine. Panettiere told the On Purpose podcast, "I think there's been this very common misconception that I just gave up my child. That could not be farther from the truth."

Panettiere said Klitschko suggested their daughter live with him full-time when Kaya was 2. She said she was in a "horrible cycle for years of battling depression and anxiety and alcoholism and substance abuse."

In a statement shared to Instagram after Panettiere's death, Klitschko wrote, "The announcement of Hayden's tragic death saddens me deeply. She left this world far too soon. Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya."

Why has there been backlash against Neutrogena?

Panettiere was a longtime spokesperson for Neutrogena , appearing in commercials for the skin care brand for more than a decade. She alleged that the company wanted to end their relationship after she spoke publicly about experiencing postpartum depression in 2015.

"Of all the things… that they would fire me over, this was the last thing I thought they would fire me over," Panettiere told On Purpose.

Panettiere said her representative intervened and she was not immediately dropped, but that her relationship with the company subsequently ended.

"I'd worked with these people for 10 years, and I remember not hearing a word from anybody, not a 'great working with you for 10 years,' 'hope you're good; we wish you well.' And I remember that really breaking my heart."

Her allegations drew criticism of Neutrogena when they became public in May and resurfaced following her death, with some social media users calling for a boycott of the brand.

"For more than a decade, Hayden was a valued member of our Neutrogena community," Neutrogena said after her death. "We are proud to have partnered with her and understand that we made her feel unsupported during a very difficult time. This is not what Neutrogena stands for or who we want to be."

What else did she say in her recent memoir?

Panettiere released her memoir in May, three months before her death. The book traced her life from child stardom through some of her most difficult years, including her struggles with addiction and the death of her younger brother, Jansen, in 2023.

She wrote about how closely her own life began to mirror that of her Nashville character, Juliette Barnes, whose storylines included postpartum depression and problems with alcohol and pills. At the time, Panettiere was dealing with anxiety and addiction herself, writing that she eventually reached a point where she "needed a drink to function."

"Every time I read the day's script, it was like I was looking in a funhouse mirror, seeing a distorted reflection of myself. I can't tell you how lost this made me feel," she wrote.

Panettiere described herself as a "work in progress" in the memoir. In its closing pages, she wrote, "I just keep swimming, and with each stroke, I get stronger. With each passing day, I get to laugh a little more, learn another lesson, and make another friend."

What has been said about the cause of death?

Panettiere was found in cardiac arrest after emergency responders were called to the Greenville, S.C., residence where she was temporarily staying, according to the Greenville County Coroner's Office. She was pronounced dead after attempts to resuscitate her were unsuccessful.

An autopsy found no signs of trauma that contributed to her death, the coroner's office said. Her cause and manner of death have not yet been determined and are pending additional testing.

In her memoir, Panettiere wrote about her decision to "let go of my resentment" and try to forgive Hickerson. She added, "I needed him to admit his wrongs and change because of them, but I didn't want to traumatize him in an irreversible way."

Months before her death, Panettiere had reportedly taken steps to keep Hickerson away. The New York Times reported, citing two people with direct knowledge, that private security accompanying her book tour in May had instructions not to let Hickerson into events.
"I needed an incredible amount of support and backup in order to make sure that there was no way for him to find his way back in," Panettiere told the podcast On Purpose .

Vogel described her daughter's relationship with Hickerson as codependent, saying, "When Brian came into her life, the changes started to occur. Very early in the game, I thought he's a modern-day gigolo. I know what he's after.

"I would talk to both of them about it. I would say, 'This is a codependent relationship, and it is not healthy for either of you. My sadness is that everything that I did, her father did, friends did, business people did, we could not break that codependent bond. It is so much more powerful than people understand."
Vogel told ABC News, "She knew that Brian was toxic. She knew she had to get him out of her life."
Hickerson has not been accused of a crime in connection with Panettiere's death.
Hickerson addressed Panettiere's death through his attorney, Sloan Ellis, saying, "Hayden's death remains under investigation, and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed.

"As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play. Out of respect for Hayden's loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time."
What was her relationship with the father of her child, Wladimir Klitschko?

Panettiere dated boxer Wladimir Klitschko on and off between 2009 and 2018. They got engaged in 2013 , but never married, and their daughter, Kaya, was born in 2014. Panettiere was open about her struggles with alcohol and depression, including postpartum depression after Kaya's birth.

Kaya, who is 11, lives with Klitschko in Ukraine. Panettiere told the On Purpose podcast, "I think there's been this very common misconception that I just gave up my child. That could not be farther from the truth."

Panettiere said Klitschko suggested their daughter live with him full-time when Kaya was 2. She said she was in a "horrible cycle for years of battling depression and anxiety and alcoholism and substance abuse."

In a statement shared to Instagram after Panettiere's death, Klitschko wrote, "The announcement of Hayden's tragic death saddens me deeply. She left this world far too soon. Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya."
Why has there been backlash against Neutrogena?

Panettiere was a longtime spokesperson for Neutrogena , appearing in commercials for the skin care brand for more than a decade. She alleged that the company wanted to end their relationship after she spoke publicly about experiencing postpartum depression in 2015.
"Of all the things… that they would fire me over, this was the last thing I thought they would fire me over," Panettiere told On Purpose.
Panettiere said her representative intervened and she was not immediately dropped, but that her relationship with the company subsequently ended.

"I'd worked with these people for 10 years, and I remember not hearing a word from anybody, not a 'great working with you for 10 years,' 'hope you're good; we wish you well.' And I remember that really breaking my heart."
Her allegations drew criticism of Neutrogena when they became public in May and resurfaced following her death, with some social media users calling for a boycott of the brand.

"For more than a decade, Hayden was a valued member of our Neutrogena community," Neutrogena said after her death. "We are proud to have partnered with her and understand that we made her feel unsupported during a very difficult time. This is not what Neutrogena stands for or who we want to be."
What else did she say in her recent memoir?

Panettiere released her memoir in May, three months before her death. The book traced her life from child stardom through some of her most difficult years, including her struggles with addiction and the death of her younger brother, Jansen, in 2023.

She wrote about how closely her own life began to mirror that of her Nashville character, Juliette Barnes, whose storylines included postpartum depression and problems with alcohol and pills. At the time, Panettiere was dealing with anxiety and addiction herself, writing that she eventually reached a point where she "needed a drink to function."
"Every time I read the day's script, it was like I was looking in a funhouse mirror, seeing a distorted reflection of myself. I can't tell you how lost this made me feel," she wrote.

Panettiere described herself as a "work in progress" in the memoir. In its closing pages, she wrote, "I just keep swimming, and with each stroke, I get stronger. With each passing day, I get to laugh a little more, learn another lesson, and make another friend."
What has been said about the cause of death?

Panettiere was found in cardiac arrest after emergency responders were called to the Greenville, S.C., residence where she was temporarily staying, according to the Greenville County Coroner's Office. She was pronounced dead after attempts to resuscitate her were unsuccessful.
An autopsy found no signs of trauma that contributed to her death, the coroner's office said. Her cause and manner of death have not yet been determined and are pending additional testing.

articles.title: Raksha Bandhan 2026: Date, purnima tithi, shubh muhurat, Rakhi timings and puja vidhi
articles.summary: Trending News: Rakhi season is almost here. The Rakhis are out, sweet shops are getting busier and families are already making plans for that one special morning whe.
articles.body: Rakhi season is almost here. The Rakhis are out, sweet shops are getting busier and families are already making plans for that one special morning when brothers and sisters sit together for the ceremony.Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on Friday, August 28, 2026. The festival, also known as Rakhi, falls on the full moon day, or Purnima Tithi, of the Hindu month of Shravana.If you're wondering when to tie the Rakhi, what the shubh muhurat is and what you need for the traditional puja, here's a simple guide.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Date and Purnima TithiAccording to Drik Panchang, Raksha Bandhan falls on August 28, 2026.The Purnima Tithi begins at 9:08 am on August 27 and ends at 9:48 am on August 28.There's a reason you may find slightly different Rakhi timings online. Hindu festival timings are worked out according to the local sunrise and other Panchang calculations, so the muhurat isn't necessarily identical in every city.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Shubh MuhuratFor New Delhi, the Rakhi-tying muhurat on August 28 is from 5:57 am to 9:48 am.That's a little over three and a half hours, giving families plenty of time to get together and perform the ceremony.The Bhadra period ends before sunrise in New Delhi on August 28, so it doesn't overlap with this Rakhi-tying window.If you're celebrating outside Delhi, though, check the Panchang for your own city before deciding on the timing.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Rakhi-Tying TimingsThe timing changes slightly depending on the city.In Mumbai, for instance, the Rakhi-tying muhurat is 6:22 am to 9:48 am on August 28, according to Drik Panchang.You might also see Choghadiya timings listed for the day. But those shouldn't automatically be taken as the Rakhi-tying muhurat. The two aren't necessarily the same.And if your family traditionally avoids Rahu Kaal for auspicious ceremonies, remember that this timing also depends on the city.Mumbai Raksha Bandhan 2026 TimingsRaksha Bandhan: Friday, August 28, 2026Rakhi-tying muhurat: 6:22 am to 9:48 amPurnima Tithi begins: August 27 at 9:08 amPurnima Tithi ends: August 28 at 9:48 amBhadra: Ends before sunrise on August 28These are Mumbai-specific timings. If you're celebrating somewhere else, use the Panchang for your city.Raksha Bandhan 2026: Puja VidhiThe actual Rakhi ceremony is pretty straightforward.After the morning bath and other daily rituals, the family can get the puja thali ready. Usually, it includes the Rakhi, roli or kumkum, akshat, a diya and some sweets.The brother sits down for the ceremony and the sister applies a tilak to his forehead, followed by akshat. She then performs the aarti and prays for his health, happiness and long life.Then comes the moment everyone is waiting for - she ties the Rakhi around his wrist and offers him sweets.The brother traditionally gives his sister a gift in return. And, depending on the family, there may be hugs, teasing, photographs and a lot of catching up afterwards.That's also why there isn't one rigid way to celebrate Raksha Bandhan. Customs can differ from family to family and region to region. Some keep the ceremony elaborate, while others prefer a quick puja followed by lunch together.At the heart of it, though, the idea remains the same: a day to celebrate the bond between siblings.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: "El Cacas" Kenia Os se confiesa con Rosalía en concierto de CDMX
articles.standfirst: La cantante mexicana fue invitada de lujo a la presentación de la española
articles.summary: La cantante mexicana fue invitada de lujo a la presentación de la española
articles.body: La experiencia de los conciertos de la cantante española, Rosalía, no se remiten únicamente a vivir e interpretar con mucha pasión sus grandes éxitos, la realidad es que este es un espectáculo integral y una de las dinámicas que no solamente el público que asiste disfruta, sino que además de vuelve viral pronto en redes sociales es la del llamado ‘Confesionario’, en donde la también compositora invita a otra celebridad que saca a la luz un tema escabroso de su vida personal y en su primera presentación en la Ciudad de México, el turno fue para una colega suya, Kenia Os. La nacida en Mazatlán, Sinaloa, el 15 de julio de 1999 (27 años de edad), cuyo nombre real es Kenia Guadalupe Flores Osuna, ha literalmente encendido las redes sociales y es que ha hecho público una infidelidad de la que fue víctima hace algún tiempo, no sabemos cuándo y no sabemos exactamente a quién se refiere, pero si tenemos una gran e interesante especulación, pero primera, repasemos que fue lo que dijo y que tiene a todo el mundo atentos al chisme. “Ninguna de mis relaciones ha funcionado porque soy una mujer que pongo límites, digo lo que no me gusta y, bueno, todo este tipo de cosas que me hacen ser una mala mujer, obviamente, sabes”, dijo Kenia Os en el Palacio de los Deportes el pasado sábado por la noche. “Hoy vamos a hablar de un cacas”. “Yo estaba en un tour, yo iba a dejar el país por bastantes semanas, era un tour muy importante, mi tour por primera vez en Estados Unidos. Entonces, como buenas personas, cantantes que se están conociendo, nos prometimos paz, tranquilidad, armonía, nada de cosas turbias, lo típico”, aseveró durante el evento que corresponde al LUX Tour 2026. “De repente me doy cuenta que él etiqueta a una mujer, en oculto. ¿Cómo me di cuenta? Tengo muchas amigas y muchos gays. Obviamente le pregunté por qué etiquetarla en oculto, no me hablaste nada de ella. No me quiero ver loca, pero necesito un poquito mi espacio porque nos estamos conociendo, como buen hombre me dijo: ‘Nada que ver’, ‘estás loca, ni al caso’, ‘jamás andaría con ella’. Acto seguido, en ese tiempo que nos estábamos dando, tiempo muy corto, o sea, como 10 días, comienza a salir con ella”.

articles.summary:
In the latest study, at least 215 of 878 former players suffered from chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), but the number is likely much higher:
> The total does not include several other brains examined by scientists not affiliated with the researchers, and thus unverifiable, or those widely presumed to have had CTE due to the severity of symptoms but who were not tested at death.

articles.title: âVijayakanth is the reason we eat well todayâ: MS Bhaskar gets emotional remembering Vijayakanth on the late actorâs 74th birth anniversary
articles.summary: Vijayakanth continues to hold a special place in the hearts of Tamil cinema fans and artistes. On his 74th birth anniversary, several people visited h.
articles.body: Vijayakanth continues to hold a special place in the hearts of Tamil cinema fans and artistes. On his 74th birth anniversary, several people visited his memorial to remember the late actor and politician. Actor MS Bhaskar was one of those who paid tribute, and he got emotional while speaking about his bond with Vijayakanth. His words showed that the late actorâs support was not just professional but also had a deep impact on his personal life.MS Bhaskar recalls Vijayakanth as his elder brotherAfter paying his respects at the memorial, MS Bhaskar spoke to media about Vijayakanth. âVijayakanth was our elder brother. He was like a mother who fed me and brought me up,â he said, as reported by Filmibeat. MS Bhaskar added that although Vijayakanth may have left the world physically, his memories continue to remain alive among those who loved him. He also noted the large number of people who had gathered at the memorial, saying their presence showed the affection they still have for the late actor.MS Bhaskar gets emotional about Vijayakanthâs kindnessBhaskar also remembered Vijayakanth for his caring nature and his concern for people around him. âHe always wanted everyone to eat well. Even now, annadhanam is being organised at his memorial. Though he has left us physically, he has not left us in our hearts,â he said. He further added, âEveryone who has come here has great affection for him.â His words recalled Vijayakanthâs reputation for helping people in the film industry and ensuring that those around him were treated with care and respect.MS Bhaskar hails Vijayakanth for his successThe most emotional moment came when Bhaskar spoke about how Vijayakanth had personally helped his family. âIf my family and I are able to eat well three times a day today, Vijayakanth is the reason for it,â he said. Vijayakanth, who passed away in December 2023, had built a career spanning more than 100 films before entering politics. He was also known for supporting fellow artistes and technicians. As tributes poured in on his birth anniversary, MS Bhaskarâs words offered a touching reminder of the lives Vijayakanth had quietly influenced.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Abhay Verma on his equation with contemporaries Ahaan Panday, Aneet Padda and Vedang Raina: 'No competition among us'
articles.summary: Abhay Verma has opened up about his equation with contemporaries Ahaan Panday, Aneet Padda and Vedang Raina, making it clear that competition has no p.
articles.body: Abhay Verma has opened up about his equation with contemporaries Ahaan Panday, Aneet Padda and Vedang Raina, making it clear that competition has no place among the young crop of actors in the industry. He heaped praise on his peers, especially Aneet Padda, with whom he shares a long-standing friendship.Abhay Verma praises Ahaan Panday and Vedang RainaTalking about Ahaan Panday and Aneet Padda's success with 'Saiyaara' and Vedang Raina's acclaim for 'Main Vaapas Aaunga', Abhay Verma told News18 Showsha, "I've met Ahaan a couple of times. He's a lovely guy. I really respect him. Kudos to him and Aneet for breaking records with Saiyaara! I hope they do it with many more films. I wish the same for Vedang."Abhay Verma talks about his six-year bond with Aneet PaddaAbhay Verma shared that his friendship with Aneet Padda goes back several years, having first met her on the sets of a commercial. He said, "Aneet and I go back a long way, roughly six years. We did a Cadbury commercial, and we hit it off. She's from Amritsar, and I'm from Panipat, which are [culturally] very similar. She has a great sense of humour, and that's where we bonded. I'm so proud of her. She's a beautiful actor. There's no way she didn't deserve the love that came her way. She deserves all of it and more," he said.Speaking about the camaraderie among young actors today, Abhay said, "I believe that we, young actors, don't really have that sense of competition among us. We respect each other's dreams. We know the kind of stakes that are on us and the value of opportunities. That's why we respect the opportunities each of us gets."He added, "We're all here to serve a bigger purpose, which is to entertain the audience. What we've among us is beautiful. I speak to all them. I was recently speaking to Pratibha [Ranta], Rohit [Saraf] and Bhuvan [Bam] about The Revolutionaries."More about Abhay VermaOn the work front, he will next feature in Siddharth Anand's 'King' starring Shah Rukh Khan. The movie also features Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan, Arshad Warsi, Suhana Khan, Arshad Warsi, Saurabh Shukla, and more. The film is slated to hit theatres in December this year.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.summary: Fallece la legendaria cantante.
articles.body: La legendaria cantante y compositora de música country Dolly Parton se despidió de los años 80, según anunció su familia. Su muerte fue anunciada por su sobrino Brian Seaver en Instagram. "Me imaginaba la tristeza de este momento, pero no la había sentido de verdad hasta ahora", dijo. "Es un homenaje, un homenaje que combina un orgullo absoluto con una profunda tristeza". Dolly Parton nació el 19 de enero de 1946 en Pittman Center, Tennessee, y creció en una familia numerosa en una cabaña de una sola habitación. Era una de doce hermanos, y su crianza en la zona rural de Tennessee se convirtió en una importante fuente de inspiración para sus composiciones. Su talento musical se manifestó a una edad muy temprana. De niña, actuaba en la televisión local y se presentó en el Grand Ole Opry de Nashville con tan solo 13 años. Tras graduarse de la escuela secundaria en 1964, Parton se mudó a Nashville y comenzó a forjar su carrera como compositora e intérprete. Su colaboración con Porter Wagoner la consolidó como una gran estrella de la música country, pero Parton finalmente se independizó para seguir su propio camino. Esta transición dio lugar a algunas de las canciones que definirían su legado, como Jolene y I Will Always Love You. La influencia de Parton superó con creces los límites tradicionales de la música country. Su éxito de 1980, "9 to 5", fue un gran éxito pop y, además, dio título a la película que protagonizó junto a Jane Fonda y Lily Tomlin. Posteriormente, apareció en películas como "Magnolias de acero" y "La mejor casa de putas de Texas". También fue una de las compositoras más exitosas comercialmente de la música estadounidense. Reuters informó que Parton vendió más de 100 millones de discos en todo el mundo, y 25 de sus canciones alcanzaron el número 1 en la lista de éxitos country de Billboard. Ganó 11 premios Grammy, incluyendo un premio a la trayectoria, y fue incluida en el Salón de la Fama del Rock & Roll en 2022. "I Will Always Love You" se convirtió en una canción particularmente significativa para su legado. Parton la escribió originalmente como una despedida a Wagoner, pero la exitosa versión de Whitney Houston la dio a conocer a otra generación y la convirtió en uno de los sencillos más exitosos comercialmente jamás grabados por una artista femenina. Los logros de Parton también se extendieron al mundo empresarial. Transformó un parque temático de Tennessee en Dollywood, que se convirtió en un importante destino turístico y una fuerza económica significativa en la región. Quizás su contribución más perdurable fuera del mundo del espectáculo fue la Biblioteca de la Imaginación de la Fundación Dollywood. Esta iniciativa de alfabetización, establecida en 1995, proporcionaba libros gratuitos a niños pequeños y, con el tiempo, se expandió más allá de Tennessee a varios países. El programa ha distribuido más de 150 millones de libros, según The Guardian. Parton también donó un millón de dólares para la investigación de la vacuna contra la COVID-19 en la Universidad de Vanderbilt en 2020, convirtiéndose en una importante patrocinadora financiera de la investigación vinculada al desarrollo de la vacuna de Moderna. Sus últimos años estuvieron marcados por nuevos proyectos. Su sitio web oficial destacó recientemente las certificaciones de su nueva música y una producción de Broadway, DOLLY: A True Original Musical, cuyo estreno estaba previsto para diciembre de 2026. Hasta el momento, la familia no ha confirmado la causa de la muerte de Dolly Parton. Sin embargo, la cantante había enfrentado severon problemas de salud en los últimos meses. Parton anunció repentinamente en mayo de 2026 que cancelaba un espectáculo en Las Vegas y añadio había estado recibiendo tratamiento para cálculos renales durante varios años. La muerte de Parton cierra uno de los capítulos más notables del entretenimiento estadounidense moderno. Logró desenvolverse con éxito entre la música country, el pop, el cine, la televisión, los negocios y la filantropía, manteniendo siempre una conexión con sus raíces de Tennessee, que la moldearon. Para generaciones de fans, su voz inconfundible, sus composiciones y su generosidad serán inseparables de la historia de la música estadounidense.

articles.title: There was only one Dolly Parton. See her remarkable life in photos.
articles.summary: Parton was the purest kind of pop icon, with an image and a sound that was universally beloved yet entirely her own.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton died in Nashville on Tuesday at the age of 80 , but her outsize legacy will live on. Over a peerless six-decade career as a country singer, songwriter, entertainer and entrepreneur, Parton transmuted her hardscrabble roots as the daughter of an illiterate Tennessee sharecropper into the purest kind of pop iconography: an image and a sound that was universally beloved yet entirely her own.

In 2019, the New York Times ran a story with the headline "Is There Anything We Can All Agree On?" The answer? "Yes: Dolly Parton."

Among the things that everyone agreed on was Parton's prodigious talent. A child performer on local radio and television programs, she first broke through, in 1966, with a single called "Dumb Blonde." "Just because I'm blonde, don't think I'm dumb," Parton sang in the chorus. "'Cause this dumb blonde ain't nobody's fool."

The song was written by someone else, but the sentiment would come to define Parton's layered public persona: a voluptuous, rhinestone-studded, bouffant-bewigged " Backwoods Barbie " who happened to be the shrewdest of businesswomen, the sharpest of lyricists and the most generous of philanthropists.

"I've created this and played it up — the makeup, the whole persona," Parton said in a 2002 interview . "But this isn't all I am. It's not even most of what I am. Hopefully people can see beneath the hair to know there's a brain, beneath the boobs to know there's a heart and behind all the other stuff to know there's some talent."

Parton penned most of her subsequent hits herself. She found early success duetting with fellow country singer Porter Wagoner, but struck out on her own in the mid-1970s after a string of solo singles — " Joshua ," " Coat of Many Colors ," " Touch Your Woman ," My Tennessee Mountain Home ," "Travelin' Man," "Jolene" — made the country Top 20.

In 1974, Parton wrote "I Will Always Love You" about her professional split from Wagoner; the song was a hit for Parton multiple times (1974, 1982, 1995), and eventually topped the charts for 14 weeks when Whitney Houston covered it for The Bodyguard soundtrack in 1992.

All told, Parton was the top-ranking female singer on country radio from 1967 to 1993, with a total of 25 No. 1 country singles. She published 3,000 songs in her lifetime, blazing a trail for other women along the way. "I can't imagine anybody, especially in country, who doesn't try to emulate Dolly in some way," singer-songwriter Emmylou Harris said in 2006.

The fact that Parton accomplished so much in music while also challenging cultural stereotypes, starring in movies, opening a theme park, funding education programs and emphasizing hope, resilience, empathy and acceptance, both on stage and off — it all made her easy to agree on. It's hard to imagine that anyone else could have pulled it off, or will ever come close again.

articles.title: Dolly Parton has died at 80.
articles.summary:
Her family announced that Parton died peacefully at home today in Nashville, TN. A singer, songwriter, actress, entrepreneur, and philanthropist, among a long list of other titles, she released over 3,000 songs and has sold over 100 million records.
Parton also donated $1 million in 2020 to assist in the early development of Moderna’s coronavirus vaccine, and the family has asked that donations in her memory go to her Imagination Library, which has distributed more than 332 million books to help young children learn to read.

articles.title: Dolly Parton dead at 80: Tributes, photos and reactions pour in from around the world
articles.summary: Reactions and remembrances are pouring in following news of the beloved country music icon's passing.
articles.body: Reactions and remembrances are pouring in following the death of Dolly Parton, the beloved country music icon, at age 80.Bryan Seaver, Parton's nephew and head of security for more than two decades, announced the news of her death on Instagram. A rep for the singer later issued a statement to People revealing that she had “bravely [faced] a brief battle with cancer.”"Dolly opened doors for singers, songwriters, musicians and dreamers from every walk of life," Seaver said. "By her example, we believed anything was possible.""She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD, and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family, whether you liked it or not," he added. "Our family and the team she has entrusted with her legacy will work diligently to ensure her spirit will live with us forever."Tributes poured in over the course of the day, with legends from the worlds of music, movies, TV and even politics sharing how much Parton inspired them with her talent, perseverance and, above all, her open heart. Parton's death comes after she announced in May that she was canceling her Las Vegas residency, which was set to begin in September after already being postponed nine months. She cited unspecified health issues but told the public in a video on Instagram that she was "responding really well to meds and treatments" and "improving every day."Follow below for updates, remembrances and more.

articles.title: Katey Sagal Marks 40 Years of Sobriety With Family and ‘These 3 Loves of My Life’
articles.summary: Katey Sagal marked 40 years of continuous sobriety with a garden party that kept the milestone close to home. The 72-year-old actress celebrated on Saturday,...
articles.body:
Katey Sagal marked 40 years of continuous sobriety with a garden party that kept the milestone close to home.

The 72-year-old actress celebrated on Saturday, August 22, surrounded by friends, husband Kurt Sutter and her three children, according to PEOPLE's account of the gathering . She shared photographs from the celebration the following day.

In her Instagram caption , Sagal called Sarah Grace White, Jackson White and Esme Sutter "these 3 loves of my life" and said she was "grateful beyond," adding, "It's a wonderful life."

The family celebration came four decades after Sagal got sober in 1986, shortly before the role that transformed her career on Married... with Children . In recent interviews, she has spoken candidly about how small her life once felt, why recovery initially sounded almost too good to believe and how sobriety later influenced her own son.

Sagal Celebrated With Her Husband and All Three Children

Sagal's photographs showed an outdoor celebration beneath string lights, with a table covered in desserts, flowers and a large cake. All three of her children were visible in the photographs. Entertainment Weekly reported that Jackson and Esme stood together applauding while Sarah photographed her mother from the side.

Sutter, whom Sagal married in 2004, was also part of the celebration. Sagal described the gathering as one surrounded by "like minded friends," her "amazing husband" and her children.

Jackson White Says His Mother's Recovery Showed Him Change Was Possible

Sagal's sobriety eventually became more than her own story. Her son Jackson White, now 30, has said watching his mother rebuild her life provided an example when he later confronted his own relationship with alcohol.

During a February appearance on Call Her Daddy , the Tell Me Lies actor said Sagal had gotten her life together long before he faced the same decision. "She got her s--- together a long time ago," Jackson said. "I got to see that you can get your s--- together."

He called his mother a "really great example" and said his own life changed substantially after he stopped drinking. Jackson has spoken separately about drinking from a young age with his late father, drummer Jack White, and realizing that alcohol could eventually control his life if he did not change direction.

Sagal Says Her Life Before Recovery Had Become 'Very, Very Small'

Sagal offered one of her most recent reflections on those earlier years during an August 5 appearance on Where Everybody Knows Your Name with Ted Danson.

She said much of her drinking and drug use had been connected to rigid expectations about what her life was supposed to become. When those plans failed to materialize, substances became a way of shutting out the disappointment. "My life was very, very small," she said.

Sagal contrasted that period with the life she eventually built through recovery: acting, raising children, relationships and experiences she had not imagined while narrowly defining success around becoming a rock star. The change was difficult for her to believe when she first entered recovery.

She remembered being told that she was "dreaming too small" and that her life could become better than she imagined if she stayed sober. At the time, she admitted, the promise sounded like "a sales pitch." "With my recovered state, recovery state, my life is pretty big in a great way," she told Danson decades later.

She Was Only Four Months Sober When Peg Bundy Came Along

Sagal entered one of the defining periods of her career while her sobriety was still extremely new. In a 2025 conversation with Neal Brennan , she said she had been sober for only four months when she got Married... with Children .

She was frightened because she had never approached a major acting job without relying on substances in some form. A sponsor advised her to tell someone at work that she was sober. Sagal reluctantly followed that advice and discovered that one of the first people she confided in was also in recovery.

Knowing there was someone else on the set who understood what she was experiencing provided a sense of safety at a moment when she felt particularly exposed.

The job became anything but temporary. Sagal played Peggy Bundy opposite Ed O'Neill for all 11 seasons of the Fox sitcom, from 1987 to 1997, turning a role she began only months into sobriety into one of the performances most closely associated with her career.

She Says Sobriety Forced Her to Stop Numbing Difficult Experiences

Sagal has been equally direct about what recovery did not do, it did not remove grief, fear or other painful parts of life. During a 2025 appearance on Christina Applegate and Jamie-Lynn Sigler's MeSsy podcast, she said she began using drugs and alcohol at 15 and spent many years medicating herself rather than processing what happened to her.

She pointed to major experiences including losing both of her parents and having cancer in her 20s, saying she did not truly deal with much of what she went through at the time. Once she stopped using substances, avoidance was no longer available in the same way. "The brave part of living a sober life is that life's f---ing terrifying," Sagal said.
