Sagal contrasted that period with the life she eventually built through recovery: acting, raising children, relationships and experiences she had not imagined while narrowly defining success around becoming a rock star. The change was difficult for her to believe when she first entered recovery.

She remembered being told that she was "dreaming too small" and that her life could become better than she imagined if she stayed sober. At the time, she admitted, the promise sounded like "a sales pitch." "With my recovered state, recovery state, my life is pretty big in a great way," she told Danson decades later.
She Was Only Four Months Sober When Peg Bundy Came Along

Sagal entered one of the defining periods of her career while her sobriety was still extremely new. In a 2025 conversation with Neal Brennan , she said she had been sober for only four months when she got Married... with Children .

She was frightened because she had never approached a major acting job without relying on substances in some form. A sponsor advised her to tell someone at work that she was sober. Sagal reluctantly followed that advice and discovered that one of the first people she confided in was also in recovery.
Knowing there was someone else on the set who understood what she was experiencing provided a sense of safety at a moment when she felt particularly exposed.

The job became anything but temporary. Sagal played Peggy Bundy opposite Ed O'Neill for all 11 seasons of the Fox sitcom, from 1987 to 1997, turning a role she began only months into sobriety into one of the performances most closely associated with her career.
She Says Sobriety Forced Her to Stop Numbing Difficult Experiences

Sagal has been equally direct about what recovery did not do, it did not remove grief, fear or other painful parts of life. During a 2025 appearance on Christina Applegate and Jamie-Lynn Sigler's MeSsy podcast, she said she began using drugs and alcohol at 15 and spent many years medicating herself rather than processing what happened to her.

She pointed to major experiences including losing both of her parents and having cancer in her 20s, saying she did not truly deal with much of what she went through at the time. Once she stopped using substances, avoidance was no longer available in the same way. "The brave part of living a sober life is that life's f---ing terrifying," Sagal said.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Died After a ‘Brief Battle with Cancer,’ Her Team Confirms
articles.summary: The country music legend died at 80 on Tuesday, Aug. 25
articles.body:
Dolly Parton's cause of death has been revealed

Her nephew Bryan Seaver announced her death in an Instagram video on Tuesday, Aug. 25

Parton acknowledged her health struggles just days before her passing but expressed her determination to keep working

Dolly Parton 's official cause of death has been determined.

In a statement to PEOPLE on Tuesday, Aug. 25, reps for the country star confirmed the "Jolene" singer died after being diagnosed with cancer.

"Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched. Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand," the statement read.

"Whether it be the hundreds of millions of books donated through her invaluable Imagination Library or funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world, Dolly's unconditional love for all people was the guiding force for her lasting impact. After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones," the statement concluded.

Parton died at 80 on Aug. 25 . Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, announced the news in an Instagram video the same day.

Parton was admitted to a Nashville-area hospital on Friday, Aug. 21, where she died four days later.

In his Instagram video to share the news of Parton's death, Seaver began by introducing himself.

"My name is Bryan Seaver, son of Cassie Parton, and I'm representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next," he says in the video.

"This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality," he continued. "As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven't truly felt it until now."

Seaver added: "It is an honor, an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly. Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents and countless others who have watched her and longed to meet her in the heavens."

On Friday, Aug. 21, just four days before her death, Parton herself acknowledged her recent health decline .

"As I've shared in video messages throughout the past year, I am dealing with some health issues that I just didn't pay attention to when I was watching over [my husband] Carl. You know, this isn't the first time I've had to manage something like this. Back in the early '80s, I was down for several months with female issues, and I was struggling with my weight at the time too, so it's not like I haven't been through hard times with my health," Parton told PEOPLE.

She added: "But I think because we live in a 24/7 world with social media, everything gets magnified in ways it wasn't years ago. I used to joke that I was the Queen of the Tabloids, but now I guess I can say I'm the Queen of Social Media AI! Seriously, though, even though I'm still healin', I'm still workin'! You know me — as I've often said — I've dreamed myself into a corner and I still have so many things I want to achieve, so I'm gonna keep on working as long as I can to see everything come to life."

With a distinguished career that lasted decades, Parton is the best-selling female country music artist of all time, having sold more than 160 million albums worldwide. Her debut album was 1967's Hello, I'm Dolly , and she went on to release a slew of hits, including "I Will Always Love You," "9 to 5" and "Jolene."

Parton was pre-deceased by her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean , in March of 2025.

At the time, Parton announced his death on Instagram, writing, "Carl and I spent many wonderful years together. Words can't do justice to the love we shared for over 60 years."

During their long marriage, Dean opted to stay out of the spotlight but encouraged his wife. "He's always supporting me as long as I don't try to drag him in on it," Parton once told PEOPLE . "He's always been my biggest fan behind the scenes, but he's at home. I don't think they're probably showing much of this on TV, and if they do, he might see it."

"I always joke and laugh when people ask me what's the key to my long marriage and lasting love," Parton also told PEOPLE in 2018. "I always say 'Stay gone!' and there's a lot of truth to that. I travel a lot, but we really enjoy each other when we're together and the little things we do."

articles.title: Remember This Banger: Pedro Infante's 'Cien Años' is out of this world
articles.summary: One writer's quest, with the help of notable singer-songwriters, to understand what makes Pedro Infante's "Cien Años" feel otherworldly.
articles.body:
I still remember the moment when I heard "Cien Años" for the first time. I can vividly recall the haunting aftertaste, the glorious specificity of the experience.

I had moved from Buenos Aires to Los Angeles, and somehow managed to make a living writing about Latin music. I'd seen Los Tigres del Norte in concert, shared a lengthy conversation with Vicente Fernández outside the Arrowhead Pond of Anaheim, and spent months poring through the songbook of José Alfredo Jiménez. But listening to the 1953 recording of "Cien Años" by Mexican legend Pedro Infante was a game changer — an existential milestone that will stay with me for the rest of my life.

I was in my home office, researching a story about the golden era of Mexican music. "Cien Años" played on, the elusive contours of its melody floating in the afternoon air. Three minutes and 33 seconds later, when it ended, you could hear a pin drop. I sat still for a few minutes, transfixed. Then I played it again. And again. Ten, 15, 20 times in a row.

A composition by Rubén Fuentes and Alberto Cervantes, the song wasn't just another lilting ranchera from the 1950s — that much was clear. On the contrary, it felt like an otherworldly manifestation from the gods above, as if a UFO had landed in the Mexican capital decades ago, and an advanced race of extraterrestrials left this artifact behind as some sort of exquisite offering — a reminder of everything that could be but wasn't.

There's the matter of that sinuous electric guitar intro, halfway between tropical psychedelia and merry-go-round anthem. Then, the main melody: forlorn, hallucinogenic. Infante's aristocratic delivery collides head on with the brutal indifference of the girl he will carry on loving for the rest of his embittered existence. His voice, so soft and fragile, could belong to both man and woman; the universal scar of romantic rejection.

Clearly there was a mystery attached to this evergreen standard that people got to see on the big screen in 1954, when Infante performed it in the film "Cuidado Con El Amor." The song also reminded me of Schubert — maybe a page off "Winterreise," the romantic song cycle composed in 1827.

Had I accidentally discovered a supernatural portal where time and space didn't exist, one where random phenomena of blinding beauty could materialize on this plane without any logical explanation?

To figure out why "Cien Años" still resonates, I decided to consult with a few notable singer-songwriters.

First I thought of Spanish rock star and longtime Los Angeles resident Enrique Bunbury, who himself traffics in the diffuse territories of the ominous and esoteric. I sent him a rambling voice memo, trying to convey my bewilderment as best as I could. True to his character, he replied with a terse but eloquent text.

"I apologize for the delay in responding, as I was busy promoting my new album," he wrote. "I have to agree that Pedro Infante's version has an incredibly evocative air to it that is not common in rancheras. This may be related to the classical violin training of Rubén Fuentes, who was also an arranger. Alberto Cervantes, on the other hand, was a bolero guy. I imagine he contributed the intense Acapulco scent that emanates from this song. I'm so sorry that my ignorance on this subject will probably not be of great help in your inquiry."

I marveled at Bunbury's humility, but agreed with him that the mystery was far from solved.

Maybe a young Mexican singer could shed some illumination, I thought, before sending a somewhat incoherent email to Silvana Estrada. I was right to assume that the 29-year-old prodigy behind 2025's "Vendrán Suaves Lluvias" — one of the most spiritually devastating albums of the decade, and the second best album of last year — would have something to say.

"This is one of the most gorgeous boleros in the Mexican repertoire," Estrada replied.

"I always thought the Pedro Infante version was mind-boggling. There is something in the string arrangement that sounds a bit impressionistic to me, but also profoundly Mexican, with the trumpets doubling the violin lines. There's also a sense of maximalism that sums up the old Mexico as a time of splendor. And when I think of this song, I think of something splendid."

At least now I knew that I was not alone in my overwhelming passion for this strange little gem. But neither Bunbury nor Estrada had addressed the eerie supernatural vibe that emanates from the recording — the feeling that when "Cien Años" was recorded somewhere in Mexico City, Pedro and company connected with another dimension.

I was scheduled to interview Mexican American singer Lila Downs the following day, and I decided to bring this up at the end of our chat. She was sitting down in her stately Oaxaca home when we connected over Zoom, and smiled widely the moment I brought up my metaphysical query.

"I've experienced a similar feeling with other songs that I've performed," she said. "It's like they transport me to a más allá [a far beyond], a certain undefined something that doesn't belong in my own era. 'La Llorona,' in fact, connects me to something that is not even human — a force that exists in the shape of waves. It's the essence of the very mystery that music itself evokes in all of us."

Downs pointed out an important detail: that "Cien Años" could not have emerged from any country other than Mexico.

"Our subconscious is loaded with the spirit of the ancestors," she added. "There is a deep connection with the cosmos in Mexico. I've seen it in anthropology books; this vision of art as a healing agent that facilitates spiritual growth."

I was finally ready to put the matter aside, when I spoke to Gepe. The Chilean singer-songwriter has crafted many tracks that have a timeless, soulful quality to them. "Desastre," a lovely tune released in 2024, feels almost as unearthly to me as "Cien Años."

"That intro is definitely striking," he told me in the first of many voice memos. "It has a psychedelic tinge that didn't really exist in the 1950s. It reminds me of someone like Peter Drake and his slide guitar playing, which had more of a Hawaiian sound. I think it's beautiful that such a short intro can leave you with more questions than answers. That's part of the magic, isn't it?"

Gepe made an astute observation: that my life-changing experience with "Cien Años" was not due to a single factor. It was a layered, complex combination of different details.

"You have this incredible, hypersensitive performance by Pedro, coupled with a timeless arrangement which was definitely ahead of its time," he explained. "The cinematic, almost Hawaiian touch on the guitar, but also a strong affinity to the bolero aesthetic — there's a subtle softness in the maracas, so that the voice can grow and shine with so much sweetness."

And then, he told me the one thing that brought it all together.

"It's funny, because you keep saying that this song sounds like it landed from another world, but there's a stark contradiction in that statement," he said. "Pedro's delivery is so marvelous and sensitive, that it goes beyond male or female — it sums up the human experience in all its subtlety and aching beauty. I think what happened here was that the composers, arrangers, musicians and Pedro got together in a studio and created something so immense and luminous that it ended up transcending its own sense of time."

articles.title: Dolly Parton, beloved country music icon, dies at 80 after 'brief battle with cancer'
articles.summary: Dolly Parton, the beloved singer, songwriter, actor and philanthropist, has died, her family said on Tuesday. She was 80 years old.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton, the beloved singer, songwriter, actor and philanthropist, has died, her family said on Tuesday. She was 80 years old.

In a statement issued to People , Parton's rep shared that the Queen of Country had "bravely [faced] a brief battle with cancer." She was "surrounded by loved ones" while receiving medical care at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville.

"Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched," the statement read. "Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand," the statement read.

"Whether it be the hundreds of millions of books donated through her invaluable Imagination Library or funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world, Dolly's unconditional love for all people was the guiding force for her lasting impact. After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones," the statement concluded.

In a video statement shared to Instagram on Tuesday, Parton's nephew Bryan Seaver — the son of Cassie Parton and Parton's head of security for more than two decades — shared the news that Parton had died. He said the video announcement was something that his aunt asked him to do "years ago."

"It is an honor, an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly. Dolly has lived in the light, and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents, and countless others who have watched her and longed for her to meet them in the heavens," he said.

While Seaver did not disclose details around Parton's death, he reflected on her legacy, which included opening doors for "generations of singers, songwriters, musicians, and dreamers from every walk of life and across every continent" and changing history.

"She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD, and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family, whether you liked it or not. Our family and the team she has entrusted with her legacy will work diligently to ensure her spirit will live with us forever," he continued.

"Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy. He farmed the soil. She farmed songs and happiness. Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest."

According to a post on Parton's Instagram account, "a small, private service will be held for immediate family" at the singer's request. "In lieu of flowers the family asks for donations to be made to Dolly Parton's Imagination Library at www.imaginationlibrary.com ."

President Trump on Tuesday afternoon said on social media that Parton's death "is a true loss for millions of people. There has never been anyone like her, and never will. In her honor, I am lowering the American flag throughout the United States for a one week period beginning tonight at 6:00PM. Rest in Peace, Dolly! The World loves you."

Parton's death comes after she announced in May 2026 that she was canceling her Las Vegas residency , which was set to begin in September after already being postponed nine months. She cited unspecified health issues but told the public, via Instagram video , that she was "responding really well to meds and treatments" and "improving every day."

Known as the Queen of Country , Parton built a successful career that spanned decades, during which she became one of the most honored female country performers of all time. She received 10 Grammy Awards, plus a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Primetime Emmy Award, and she holds the record for a female artist with 25 No. 1s on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart.

Parton was the fourth of 12 children born to Avie Lee Caroline Owens and Robert Lee Parton Sr., on Jan. 19, 1946, and grew up in Locust Ridge, Tenn. She often credited her uncle Bill Owens for encouraging her to pursue music after buying her a guitar and getting her a role on a television variety show in Knoxville when she was 10.

After graduating from high school in 1964, Parton moved to Nashville to pursue a career in music. She met her husband, Carl Dean, on her first day in the city , at a laundromat. The two would wed in 1966 and stay married until his death on March 3, 2025.

Parton's big break came in 1967 when Porter Wagoner asked her to replace his duet partner, Norma Jean, on the syndicated TV series The Porter Wagoner Show . The Country Music Hall of Fame credits Parton's "hourglass figure, outrageous outfits, and angelic voice" for why she performed so well as Wagoner's cohost.

Parton signed with RCA Records as both a solo artist and Wagoner's partner, and her first solo No. 1 hit was "Joshua" in 1971, which led to the success of "Jolene," "Love Is Like a Butterfly" and "I Will Always Love You" in 1974. The latter song, which she wrote in honor of Wagoner after she left his show earlier that year, would go on to become a No. 1 pop hit when Whitney Houston covered it in 1992 for The Bodyguard soundtrack.

Parton herself crossed over to the pop charts with her recording of "Here You Come Again" in 1977. Her song "9 to 5" was the title song of the film of the same name and marked Parton's film debut in 1980, starring alongside Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda. The song won two Grammys and was Oscar-nominated. She starred in a number of films, including The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas with Burt Reynolds in 1982 and Steel Magnolias with Sally Field and Julia Roberts in 1989.

She also opened Dollywood — a theme park that became a significant tourist attraction and helped fund her nonprofit Dollywood Foundation, which supports local schools and scholarship programs — in East Tennessee in 1986. The foundation launched Imagination Library in 1995, and the program now mails millions of free books to children in multiple countries.

Parton was philanthropic in many ways. After the 2016 Sevier County wildfires, the My People Fund raised and distributed more than $12 million. Parton also donated $1 million to Vanderbilt University Medical Center, connected to COVID-19 vaccine research.

Parton would go back to her roots and record several bluegrass albums throughout the early 2000s, after being inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1999. She founded her own label, Dolly Records, in 2007 and wrote the music and lyrics for the Broadway adaptation of 9 to 5 , earning her a Tony Award nomination in 2009.

The honors continued throughout her life. The Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award came in 2011, after a Kennedy Center Honors award in 2006. In 2022, she was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and in 2025 won the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

In later years, Parton dealt with health issues that forced her to pull out of public events. She didn't attend a Dollywood event in September 2025, after being diagnosed with an infection related to a kidney stone. Later that month, she announced she had to postpone her Las Vegas residency over "health challenges." In May 2026, she canceled the residency, slated for September 2026, citing undisclosed health issues and treatment that left her unable to perform.

Parton never had children of her own but is survived by several siblings and nieces and nephews. In 2014, she spoke to People about her relationship with her siblings and their kids. "I grew up in a big old family with eight kids younger than me and several of my brothers and sisters came to live with me early on in my life," she said at the time. "I've loved their kids just like they're my grandkids, and now I've got great-grand-kids!"

She added: "I often think, it just wasn't meant for me to have kids so everybody's kids can be mine."

In a statement issued to People , Parton's rep shared that the Queen of Country had "bravely [faced] a brief battle with cancer." She was "surrounded by loved ones" while receiving medical care at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville.

"Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched," the statement read. "Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand," the statement read.

"Whether it be the hundreds of millions of books donated through her invaluable Imagination Library or funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world, Dolly's unconditional love for all people was the guiding force for her lasting impact. After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones," the statement concluded.

In a video statement shared to Instagram on Tuesday, Parton's nephew Bryan Seaver — the son of Cassie Parton and Parton's head of security for more than two decades — shared the news that Parton had died. He said the video announcement was something that his aunt asked him to do "years ago."

"It is an honor, an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly. Dolly has lived in the light, and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents, and countless others who have watched her and longed for her to meet them in the heavens," he said.

While Seaver did not disclose details around Parton's death, he reflected on her legacy, which included opening doors for "generations of singers, songwriters, musicians, and dreamers from every walk of life and across every continent" and changing history.

"She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD, and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family, whether you liked it or not. "Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy. He farmed the soil. She farmed songs and happiness. Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest."

President Trump on Tuesday afternoon said on social media that Parton's death "is a true loss for millions of people. There has never been anyone like her, and never will. articles.title: 'Vishwanath and Sons' box office collection day 12 vs 'DC' Day 19: Suriya starrer records 36.6% jump; Lokesh Kanagaraj film sees 48.4% growth
articles.summary: 'Vishwanath and Sons' continued its theatrical run with an improvement in earnings on Day 12. The Suriya-starrer recorded a good rise compared with it.
articles.body: 'Vishwanath and Sons' continued its theatrical run with an improvement in earnings on Day 12. The Suriya-starrer recorded a good rise compared with its previous day's collection. According to Sacnilk, the movie earned an estimated India net of Rs 2.80 crore on its 12th day.The film had 2,854 shows on Tuesday. Its latest collection has taken the India net total to Rs 105.50 crore. The India gross collection stands at Rs 122.05 crore. Overseas earnings have reached Rs 60 crore, taking the worldwide gross to Rs 182.05 crore.'Vishwanath and Sons' sees day 12 growthThe Rs 2.80 crore collection on Day 12 represents a 36.6% increase from the Rs 2.05 crore earned on Monday. The movie recorded an overall occupancy of 23.5% across its shows.The Tamil version contributed Rs 1.55 crore to the day's India net collection. It registered an overall occupancy of 23%. The Telugu version added Rs 1.25 crore and recorded 24% occupancy.The film performed better during its later shows. Tamil screenings reached 40.85% occupancy during the night. Telugu screenings recorded 30.73% occupancy during the same period.State-wise collection of 'Vishwanath and Sons'The movie recorded an estimated India gross of Rs 3.25 crore on Day 12. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contributed Rs 1.25 crore. Tamil Nadu followed with Rs 1.40 crore.Karnataka added Rs 40 lakhs to the day's gross. Kerala contributed Rs 17 lakhs. The remaining parts of India accounted for Rs 3 lakhs.'Vishwanath and Sons' had collected Rs 81.60 crore during its first week. Its Day 7 earnings stood at Rs 4.20 crore.'DC' records 48.4% rise on Day 19'DC', featuring Lokesh Kanagaraj and Wamiqa Gabbi, also registered growth in its latest box office figures. According to Sacnilk, the movie collected an estimated India net of Rs 92 lakhs on Day 19.The Tamil film had 1,017 shows and recorded an overall occupancy of 22%. Its latest figure was 48.4% higher than the Rs 62 lakhs collected on Day 18.The Tamil version contributed Rs 72 lakhs. The Telugu version added Rs 20 lakhs. The Tamil screenings recorded 31.13% overall occupancy. Telugu screenings registered 24.02%.'DC' crosses 100 crore worldwide'DC' has so far collected Rs 67.24 crore in India net earnings. Its India gross stands at Rs 77.44 crore. The film has earned Rs 23.20 crore from overseas markets.The worldwide gross has consequently reached Rs 100.64 crore. The film had earned Rs 41.90 crore during its opening week. Its second-week collection stood at Rs 19.59 crore.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. articles.title: Arre Pepsi Black 2026 vuelve a CDMX con Alejandro Fernández en el cartel, ¿cuándo es el festival y dónde comprar los boletos?
articles.standfirst: Conoce todos los detalles sobre este magno evento de musica regional mexicana
articles.summary: Conoce todos los detalles sobre este magno evento de musica regional mexicana
articles.body: La nueva edición de Arre Pepsi Black buscará repetir el éxito que tuvo en su debut capitalino, cuando el encuentro logró convocar a más de 70 mil personas por día. Tras llevar su propuesta hasta Monterrey, el festival volverá a la Ciudad de México para reunir en un mismo escenario a grandes figuras del regional mexicano y a algunos de los exponentes que representan las nuevas generaciones del género. El regreso a la capital también marca un reencuentro con el público que acompañó al festival desde sus primeros pasos en 2023. Con una cartelera que combina nombres consolidados como Alejandro Fernández, Banda MS y Los Tucanes de Tijuana con artistas de la nueva ola, ARRE Pepsi Black apuesta nuevamente por mostrar la diversidad y evolución que atraviesa actualmente la música mexicana El Arre Pepsi Black 2026 se llevará a cabo durante dos días en la Ciudad de México: sábado 5 y domingo 6 de septiembre de 2026. El encuentro tendrá como sede el Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, donde los asistentes podrán disfrutar de una amplia selección de artistas representantes del regional mexicano. Esta nueva edición marcará el regreso del festival al recinto donde se realizaron sus primeras ediciones, por lo que los seguidores de la música mexicana podrán disfrutar nuevamente de una jornada que combinará distintos estilos y generaciones. El cartel incluye figuras como Alejandro Fernández, Banda MS y Los Tucanes de Tijuana, además de otros exponentes que completarán la programación de ambos días. Los boletos para el Arre Pepsi Black 2026 se pueden comprar a través de Ticketmaster México, donde los asistentes podrán elegir entre un abono para los dos días o una entrada individual para el sábado o domingo. Los precios proporcionados para la zona general son: El costo de las entradas puede variar conforme avance la venta y cambien las fases disponibles. Por ello, antes de realizar la compra, se recomienda consultar el precio vigente directamente en Ticketmaster, especialmente si buscas asistir a uno solo de los días o adquirir el abono completo. La cartelera del Arre Pepsi Black 2026 reúne a representantes de distintas generaciones y estilos del regional mexicano, con figuras como Alejandro Fernández, Banda MS, Los Tucanes de Tijuana, Gabito Ballesteros, Eslabón Armado, Los Dos Carnales, Grupo Cañaveral, El Mimoso, Los Plebes del Rancho, Mi Banda El Mexicano, La Sonora Dinamita, Víctor Mendivil, Calle 24 y Clave Especial. Sin embargo, estos son solo algunos de los artistas que forman parte del festival, pues el cartel completo contempla a más exponentes que se presentarán durante los dos días del evento en el Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez.

articles.title: AI-generated music barred from Australian charts after Madonna cover controversy
articles.summary: SYDNEY, Aug 26 (Reuters) - AI-generated music will be excluded from Australia's music charts starting this week, the country's peak music trade group said, f...
articles.body:
SYDNEY, Aug 26 (Reuters) - AI-generated music will be excluded from Australia's music charts starting this week, the country's peak music trade group said, ‌following controversy over an Australian DJ's cover of Madonna's "Like a Prayer" ‌topping local music charts.

The Australian Recording Industry Association, or ARIA, said on Tuesday that wholly AI-generated tracks ​would no longer be eligible for its popular ARIA Charts, although recordings that use generative AI in a supporting role would remain eligible.

A recording developed using generative AI will be eligible only if it is "substantially human made" and raises no concerns ‌around streaming or chart manipulation, ⁠ARIA said.

To distinguish AI-generated recordings from AI-assisted ones, ARIA said it would apply definitions from a labelling standard announced by the ⁠global music community in July.

Major global record labels have been seeking new licensing arrangements to protect their vast catalogues as AI-generated music grows in popularity and consumers increasingly ​struggle ​to distinguish it from human-composed songs.

"The ARIA ​charts will always remain a transparent ‌measurement of the music Australia consumes, but a chart that rewards unlicensed AI output would undercut the very basis of the recorded music we exist to represent," ARIA CEO Annabelle Herd said.

ARIA compiles Australia's most popular songs and albums in the ARIA Charts, which are released on Apple Music and Spotify every Friday.

Queensland-based ‌DJ Josh Fawaz's cover of Madonna's 1989 hit "Like ​a Prayer" became the most-played song on ​Australian radio and reached No. 4 ​on two ARIA charts in July. Some producers alleged that ‌generative AI had been used and ​that it was not ​initially disclosed.

Reuters could not immediately contact Fawaz for comment.

Responding to a music producer's criticism on Instagram in June, Fawaz said that although he used ​AI "as a tool, it's not ‌that deep", adding he had been releasing music long before AI ​and his focus was to provide his listeners "good music."

(Reporting by Renju ​Jose in Sydney; Editing by Stephen Coates)

articles.title: Dolly Parton Demonstrates How She Used Her Nails as an Instrument on the Set of “9 to 5” in Resurfaced 1981 Interview
articles.summary: “I’ve become famous for these nails,” Parton says in the clip
articles.body:
Dolly Parton used her acrylic nails to "get the rhythm" for the titular song on the set of 1980's 9 to 5

The country icon demonstrated the unique talent in a resurfaced interview clip from 1981

9 to 5 , which also starred Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda, marked Parton's acting debut

Dolly Parton was a woman of many talents.

The country legend, who died on Aug. 25 at age 80 , utilized her creativity on the set of her acting debut, the 1980 movie 9 to 5 .

In an extended 1981 interview on Sacramento's KCRA 3 , Parton demonstrated how she would rub her acrylic nails together to "get the rhythm" for the film's titular theme song.

"Ladies and gentlemen, you are now viewing the newest instrument on the market," she joked as she "played" her long red nails.

Parton explained that when she was writing the song on the movie's set, she used her nails "just to get the rhythm when I wasn't close to my guitar."

"It worked out good," she added. "So now, I've become famous for these nails."

Parton elaborated on her acrylic nail playing in an episode of Apple Fitness+ Time to Walk experience in 2021, sharing that her nails are actually credited on the 9 to 5 soundtrack.

"I thought this sounded like a typewriter, and since that movie was about women in the workplace, I'd stand on the set, I'd watch things happening, I'd come up with little lines every day," she said of writing the song. "I'd go back to my hotel room at night and get my guitar and put it down on tape until after a couple months I had a song."

She added that her nails are featured on the official recording of the song. "And I played my nails—even on the record it says 'nails by Dolly'!" she said. "Anyhow, everybody makes me do this all the time, play this little sound [of her nails like a washboard]. Of course you have to have acrylic nails, your own nails won't do that. You gotta have falsies!"

The star also shared that she had been offered several movie roles prior to 9 to 5 but turned them all down.

Jane Fonda approached Parton about the project knowing the country star would help drive a Southern audience to a movie with a mission of drawing attention to equal pay for women. With Lily Tomlin already signed on and Fonda, the film had "two big stars, so if it does good, I can take my part of the credit, and if it don't do good, I can just blame it on them," Parton recalled with a laugh. "Nobody knew me in the movies anyway!"

With Lily Tomlin already signed on and Fonda, the film had "two big stars, so if it does good, I can take my part of the credit, and if it don't do good, I can just blame it on them," Parton recalled with a laugh. "Nobody knew me in the movies anyway!"

articles.body: 'Awarapan 2' which clashed at the box office with 'Batwara 1947' ahead of Independence Day has hit the ball out of the park and how. The film which was made on a moderate budget of Rs 45 crore has gone on to earn more than 200 percent profit at the box office. It has continued its impressive run at the box office, maintaining a healthy pace even after completing its first week. The film started its theatrical journey with Rs. 22 crore on Day 1 and witnessed a significant jump on Day 2, when it collected Rs. 33.75 crore. By the end of its opening week, the sequel had earned Rs. 113.50 crore India net, while its worldwide gross stood at Rs. 161.67 crore.Awarapan 2 Movie ReviewThe film remained steady through its second weekend and also passed the second Monday test. On Day 8, it added Rs. 5.75 crore, followed by Rs. 8.25 crore on Day 9. The collection climbed further to Rs. 8.75 crore on Day 10 before dropping to Rs. 2.75 crore on Day 11.Interestingly, âAwarapan 2â witnessed an uptick on its second Tuesday, with Day 12 bringing in Rs 4 crore. The growth came amid discounted ticket prices, helping the film push its cumulative India net collection to Rs 143 crore, according to Sacnilk.The immediate challenge, however, is the increasingly crowded theatrical landscape. While âBatwara 1947â has failed to make an impact at the box office, âHanuman Anshâ has emerged as a stronger competitor in its third week. The latterâs presence could affect âAwarapan 2â further as the film is expected to lose screens with the arrival of Yash-starrer âToxicâ from today.With competition intensifying and its screen count likely to come down, the pace of âAwarapan 2â is expected to slow from here. As a result, the film may need a little more time to cross the Rs 150 crore mark, despite having built a strong foundation during its first 12 days.'Awarapan 2' also stars Disha Patani.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 'Batwara 1947' box office collection Day 12: Sunny Deol's film falls short of Rs 40 crore in India as it nears end of theatrical run, while 'Awarapan 2' races ahead, 'Toxic' to intensify competition
articles.summary: Sunny Deol-starrer 'Batwara 1947' arrived in theatres with considerable expectations, riding on the scale of the project, Aamir Khan's association as .
articles.body: Sunny Deol-starrer 'Batwara 1947' arrived in theatres with considerable expectations, riding on the scale of the project, Aamir Khan's association as a producer and Preity Zinta's return to the big screen. However, the film has struggled to translate that anticipation into box office success and is currently well short of recovering its reported budget.Batwara 1947 Movie ReviewDirected by Rajkumar Santoshi, the film opened with Rs 5.75 crore on Day 1 before witnessing a strong jump on Saturday, when it collected Rs 13.50 crore. The momentum did not sustain, with Sunday's collection dropping to Rs 7.25 crore and the first Monday bringing in just Rs 2 crore. 'Batwara 1947' eventually wrapped up its opening week with Rs 33.60 crore.The film has remained subdued in its second week as well. It added Rs 75 lakh on the second Friday, followed by Rs 1.15 crore on Saturday and Rs 1.30 crore on Sunday. The weekday collections have been particularly weak, with Day 11 bringing in only Rs 35 lakh. On the second Tuesday, Day 12, the film earned Rs 55 lakh.With these collections, 'Batwara 1947' has taken its India net total to Rs 37.70 crore. Given that the film was reportedly mounted on a budget of around Rs 120 crore, its current theatrical performance points towards a significant loss.The film's underwhelming run has also prompted trade analysts to examine why it failed to connect with audiences despite positive elements. Trade analyst Taran Adarsh recently shared his assessment with Bollywood Hungama, admitting that the film's failure surprised him.âWhat has really surprised me is why this film has not worked. In my opinion, it was a well-made film. I genuinely felt that the emotions between Shabana Azmi and Sunny Deol were very well captured on screen. The performances were of a very high order, while Rajkumar Santoshiâs direction was top-notch. The finale was very gripping. I am still unable to figure out and put a finger on why the film did not work.âAdarsh also addressed the argument that the audience may have expected Sunny Deol to deliver the kind of high-octane performance associated with his recent successes.He continued, âA lot of people told me, and I even read online, that Sunnyâs image is associated with films like Gadar (2001), Gadar 2 (2023), Jaat (2025), etc., where he is seen screaming and indulging in action. But I donât feel that Sunny was mellow over here. He was mellow only up to a point, and later, he did indulge in action. Nevertheless, it was a well-made film that did not get its due.âDespite its strong cast, experienced director and considerable production scale, 'Batwara 1947' has therefore failed to find the kind of audience response needed to turn its theatrical run into a commercial success.Meanwhile, it may now end its theatrical run with the release of Yash starrer Toxic, which will occupy major screens across the country.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' Twitter review: Yash, Kiara Advani, Nayanthara film gets mixed early reactions; netizens call it 'Heavy KGF hangover'
articles.summary: 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has arrived in theatres with huge expectations surrounding Yash's return to the big screen. Directed by Geethu Moh.
articles.body: 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has arrived in theatres with huge expectations surrounding Yash's return to the big screen. Directed by Geethu Mohandas, the action drama has started receiving reactions from audiences following its early screenings.The first responses suggest a divided opinion on Twitter space. Several viewers have praised the movie's technical presentation, production design and Yash's screen presence.Yash's performance receives praiseYash appears in a dual role in 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups'. While some viewers have questioned the narrative, his screen presence is one of the more positively discussed aspects of the movie.One viewer praised Yash's performance while expressing disappointment with the story.The user wrote, â#TOXIC FIRST HALF - BELOW PAR!! #Yash looks terrific and his charm carries the film, backed by excellent cinematography, production design and stylish action. That's it!! Story-wise, there's barely anything so far. Guns, violence, sex, fights and slow-mo moments keep coming, while the actual plot hardly moves. Visually impressive, but very much STYLE OVER SUBSTANCE so far. #ToxicReview | @Movies4u_Officl.âNetizens point to 'KGF' similaritiesSome reactions have focused on the similarities between Yash's portrayal in 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' and his popular Rocky character from the 'KGF' franchise.A viewer criticised the first half and wrote, â#TOXIC First Half: Heavy KGF Hangover! Full of violence and style, but with little substance so far. #Yash is in full-on KGF mode as Raya. Lots of bold scenes with women and too many action blocks without any real highs. Yashâs screen presence is superb. Interval block is decent.âAnother viewer took the comparison further after watching the second half, writing, â2nd half started should've named it as KGF3 instead of #Toxic #Yash #ToxicTheMovie.âScreenplay draws criticismOne viewer described the first half as disjointed and raised concerns about its action sequences and background score.The reaction read, â#Toxic Very Messy 1st Half! Apart from the technical quality, this one is all over the place so far. Heavy KGF hangover with a very clumsy and tiring screenplay. Even the action feels artificial with excessive mocobot usage, while the BGM is also a major letdown. Only the interval and a few Yash-Kiara scenes are somewhat better. The rest has been a dud so far..âAnother social media user praised the film's visual scale but found fault with its characterisation and screenplay. They wrote, â#Toxic - First Half Ultra Stylish Yash & Rich Productions Values r plus. Circus Fight Super. Has Style, Glamour, Violence. But No proper Character Intro, Dialogues, No Emotional Connect. Random Characters and a Clueless screenplay!.âEarly reactions remain dividedFurther criticism came from a viewer who felt the film prioritised spectacle over narrative substance.The user wrote, â#TOXIC First Half: Loud & Empty! All style, absolutely no substance. Not a single character makes an impact. Women, bold scenes and endless action blocks, yet NOT ONE GENUINE HIGH. The second half has a massive rescue job ahead! #ToxicReview #Yash.âAnother viewer gave the movie a 2.5/5 rating and criticised its portrayal of women. The reaction read, âTIRING 1st half #Toxic 1/2.5 It's regressive and seeing a women used as a prop just like PEDDI just to showoff the #Yash dominance is exhausting.. Monotonous Screenplay, Boring interval BREAk! #ToxicTheMovie.â'Toxic' records strong advance bookingDespite the mixed early word of mouth, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has opened with strong commercial momentum. According to Sacnilk, the movie had recorded an India Day 1 advance booking gross of Rs 64.85 crore, including block seats, as of 6 am on August 26.The movie stars Yash in a dual role, with Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria and Rukmini Vasanth in prominent roles. 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has reportedly been made on a budget of around Rs 500 crore.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.title: Dolly Partonâs Dollywood website crashes after news of âJoleneâ singerâs death is confirmed
articles.summary: Dolly Parton, the legendary singer of 'Jolene' and founder of Dollywood, has passed away at the age of 80. Following the news, her Dollywood website experienced a crash due to overwhelming traffic as fans gathered to pay tribute. Discover the legacy and impact of this musical icon.
articles.body: Within hours of confirmation that musical legend Dolly Parton had left for her heavenly abode at age 80, fans worldwide flooded her official Dollywood website. The beloved singer had founded the famous amusement park in Tennessee in 1986, turning a small tourist attraction into a fan-favourite spot for many Parton fans. Soon after, the website was flooded with traffic, causing it to malfunction.Dolly Partonâs Dollywood website goes down hours after her passingError messages flooded the official Dollywood website after news of her passing circulated online. Many fans who wished to visit the amusement parkâs website were met with a message that read, "We apologise. We are currently experiencing abnormally high volume. We appreciate your patience and hope to be back online shortly."People shared screenshots of the error message online on their social media accounts and remembered the country singer. One person on X wrote, "Of course her website would crash like thisâ¦going to miss this legend," while another shared, âDollywood website crashes today after family announces the passing of Dolly Parton." She was loved by people all around the world!âAt the time of writing, the website is up and running again and currently shares a tribute message for Dolly Parton after her passing.Country legend Dolly Parton passes away at 80Dolly Parton, who was best known for her timeless classics like 'Jolene,' âI Will Always Love You,' and âA Coat of Many Colours,' has passed away at the age of 80. The news was confirmed in a recent social media post shared on her account by her nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver. He shared the news that the icon had recently left for her heavenly abode and thanked fans for all of the love and support that she had received over the years.The post announcing her news read, "A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family. Dolly Parton's legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place. Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact."It was recently confirmed that the beloved singer had been diagnosed with cancer and had been battling the disease for some time.Give your child the gift of confidence!
